title: Your radar chart is lying by about 15%: assessment report design that people act on
summary: A radar chart encodes score as radius but your eye reads area, so a 20% gap looks like 36% — and reordering the same five scores swings the polygon 15%. How many dimensions to use, how to name the axes, where a baseline can honestly come from, and what has to sit underneath the picture.

title: The Three Types of Online Quizzes — and How to Tell Which One You Need
summary: Scored quiz, scorecard, or outcome quiz: the three types of online quizzes score differently, fail differently, and are not interchangeable. A decision table, the failure mode of each, and the four steps that settle the format before you write a single question.

title: Your quiz funnel has seven stages. You are probably watching two.
summary: There is no useful benchmark for quiz funnel conversion rate — the number depends entirely on where the traffic came from. What transfers between accounts is the shape: seven stages, five ratios, and a specific screen to open when each one sags.

title: Your quiz has no leads because nobody signed in
summary: Submissions are climbing and the Leads page is empty. That is not a bug: an anonymous submission leaves no contact details, so it creates no lead. Here is the one setting that decides it, the second door through bookings, and how to read the five-stage funnel to tell which gate you are missing.
